references.text: Jacob's dream of the ladder reaching to heaven and God's promises to him.
God's presence in a special place, Moses at the burning bush.
Job acknowledges God's presence and power after his trial.
David's realization that one cannot flee from God's presence.
Jesus referred to as 'Immanuel', which means 'God with us'.
Jesus refers to Jacob's dream of the ladder to heaven.
Both verses illustrate God's promise of presence ('I am with you') given in a nighttime revelation to patriarchs who feel alone.
A powerful contrast: Samson wakes up and does not know that the Lord has left him, while Jacob wakes up and discovers that the Lord was there all along.
Both verses capture Jacob's surprise at encountering God's presence ('God's camp'/'the Lord is in this place') and his response by naming the place.
